RESI for mgcv gam/bam: null check and point-estimate calibration

2026-11-20

  • Design
  • Null check
  • Calibration of the point estimates
    • Dependence on \(k\) (step scenario)
  • Is Ref.df the right bias correction?
  • Standard errors
  • Interpretation

Design

Simulation from tests/run_gam_calibration.R (design and decisions: notes/resi_gam.qmd). Every scenario fits

y ~ s(x1, k) + s(x2, k) + s(x3, k) + w + w0, \(k \in \{5, 10, 20\}\),

to Gaussian data with \(x_1, x_2\) uniform and correlated through a Gaussian copula (\(\rho = 0.5\), some concurvity), \(x_3\) uniform and \(w, w_0 \sim N(0, 1)\) independent. s(x3) and w0 are null.

Scenario Mean Error SD What it probes
base \(\sin(2\pi x_1) + 0.5x_2 + 0.2w\) 1 well-specified reference
step \(0.8\cdot 1(x_1 > 0.5) + 0.5x_2 + 0.2w\) 1 basis truncation error: T2 depends on \(k\)
weak_curve \(\sin(2\pi x_1) + 0.25(2x_2 - 1)^2 + 0.2w\) 1 weak non-linear effect; REML \(\hat\lambda \gg n\) at small \(n\)
hetero base \(\exp\{0.4w + 0.6(x_1 - 0.5)\}\) heteroskedasticity: parametric and robust targets differ

Each replicate draws one data set per scenario and \(n \in \{200, 1000, 5000, 20000\}\) (500 replicates). The fits are gam(method = "REML") and, in the base scenario only, bam() (fREML), each penalized (mgcv default; the estimator under evaluation) and unpenalized (fx = TRUE, a regression spline with \(k - 1\) df per smooth, for reference). Every fit is scored with two covariances:

  • Vp: mgcv’s default (parametric, Bayesian) covariance, as used by summary.gam. Smooth RESI is f2S(F, Ref.df, residual df, n); coefficient RESI is t2S(t, residual df, n).
  • sandwich: vcov.gam(sandwich = TRUE) substituted for Vp in summary.gam, same conversions.

Target. T2(k) is the Wald noncentrality per observation of the fixed-basis projection: let \(b\) be the coefficients of the population least squares projection of \(E[y \mid x]\) on the size-\(k\) (default tp) bases, \(e\) the working residual and \(A = E[XX^\top]\). Then \(S_j^2 = b_j^\top [V_{jj}]^{-1} b_j\) with

  • parametric: \(V = \sigma_k^2 A^{-1}\), \(\sigma_k^2 = E[e^2]\) (the limit of Vp), column S_T2;
  • robust: \(V = A^{-1}E[XX^\top e^2]A^{-1}\) (the limit of the sandwich), column S_T2r.

They are computed from a noiseless sample of \(2\times 10^5\), using \(E[e^2 \mid x] = \mathrm{sd}(x)^2 + \{E[y\mid x] - Xb\}^2\). Vp estimates are compared with S_T2 and sandwich estimates with S_T2r. The two coincide unless the working residual is heteroskedastic.

T2(k) targets for the non-null terms (parametric S_T2 and robust S_T2r, by k)

Calibration of the point estimates

MC mean of \(\hat S\) against \(n\) (\(k = 10\)). Solid black: parametric target S_T2; dashed black: robust target S_T2r (indistinguishable except in hetero). Error bars: \(\pm 2\) MC SE.

Dependence on \(k\) (step scenario)

With a threshold effect the basis cannot represent \(f_1\), so T2(k) increases with \(k\). The penalized estimator should track the target for its own \(k\) (horizontal lines, same colour).

Is Ref.df the right bias correction?

The \(-\text{df}\) correction removes the contribution of the estimator’s variance to \(E[T]\). On the scale used by f2S, the diagnostic is the effective df, \(E[F\,r\,(\text{rdf}-2)/\text{rdf}] - n S^2_{T2}\), compared with the MC mean of Ref.df (Vp only). Penalization also shrinks the signal part of \(T\), so a negative gap mixes a too-large df with smoothing bias. The gap divided by \(n\) is the bias of \(\hat S^2\) before truncation. The MC SE of the effective df grows like \(\sqrt{n} S\), so the check is informative only for the null and weak terms.

Standard errors

For the coefficient of \(w\), the mean SE from each covariance is compared with the MC SD of the estimate. For the smooths, Vp is a Bayesian covariance that includes the expected squared smoothing bias. Its pointwise SEs should therefore match the root MC mean squared error of \(\hat f_j\) against the fixed-basis projection, approximated here by the true \(f_j\) (exact except in step, where truncation adds a small bias). This is the across-the-function calibration of Marra & Wood (2012).

Interpretation

Numbers below are for gam, \(k = 10\), unless stated; bam matches gam in the base scenario.

  • Null check. Rejection rates for s(x3) and w0 are 0.03-0.06 in every scenario and for both covariances, including hetero. The one exception is the unpenalized fit with the sandwich at \(n = 200\) (s(x3), 0.074-0.076), the usual small-sample liberality of an HC1 sandwich with 27 parameters.
  • Both covariances are consistent for their own T2(\(k\)). By \(n = 20000\) every non-null term is within 1% of its target (2.3% for weak_curve). In hetero the two targets differ (w: 0.165 parametric vs 0.129 robust), and the Vp and sandwich estimates each converge to theirs.
  • The estimator tracks T2(\(k\)), not a basis-free value. In step, T2 for s(x1) is 0.337 / 0.355 / 0.360 for \(k\) = 5 / 10 / 20, and the mgcv estimates at \(n = 20000\) are within 0.002 of the target for their own \(k\).
  • Finite-\(n\) bias. In the base, step and hetero scenarios the penalized RESI is -3% to -17% at \(n = 200\) (largest for the small-\(S\) s(x2) and the step), -4% or less at \(n = 1000\), and under 1% from \(n = 5000\). It is less biased than the unpenalized fit with the same covariance at small \(n\).
  • Weak curve (large \(\hat\lambda\)). For the U-shaped s(x2) (\(S \approx 0.073\)), REML chose an essentially linear fit (edf < 1.1) in 49% of samples at \(n = 200\) and 10% at \(n = 1000\). The penalized RESI is -36%, -29%, -6% and -2% at \(n\) = 200, 1000, 5000, 20000. The unpenalized fit is less biased (-10% to -15% at \(n \le 1000\)) but much more variable. This is the realistic case where the penalty costs the most: a weak non-linear effect is shrunk towards the penalty null space until \(n\) is large. Both covariances behave the same here.
  • Ref.df remains an adequate bias correction (see table).
  • Standard errors. With homoskedastic errors, the w SE / MC SD is 0.97-1.05 for both covariances. Under heteroskedasticity, Vp underestimates the SD (0.72-0.82) while the sandwich is 0.92-1.00. The Vp point estimate is still consistent for the parametric target, but intervals built on Vp would undercover in hetero, as with the parametric option for other models.
